module_title: Roots of Indian Music and The Two Great Pillars
introduction: The origin of Indian classical music can be traced back to the ancient Vedic literature, specifically the **Samaveda**. Around the 13th/14th century, Indian classical music bifurcated into two distinct styles: Hindustani and Carnatic.

core_concepts.title: Hindustani Classical Music
core_concepts.description:
Region: Practiced in North, West, and Eastern India. 
Influence: Heavily influenced by Persian, Arabic, and Islamic traditions (largely due to the Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire). 
Structure: It is highly improvisational and focuses more on the vocal expression and the mood of the 'Raga'. It follows the **'Gharana'** (school/lineage) system.

core_concepts.title: Carnatic Classical Music
core_concepts.description:
Region: Practiced exclusively in South India (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh). 
Influence: Completely indigenous; it remained untouched by Persian/Islamic influences. 
Structure: It is strictly composition-based and rigid in its grammar. It emphasizes the voice over instruments. There is **NO Gharana system** in Carnatic music.

core_concepts.title: Raga and Tala
core_concepts.description:
1. **Raga:** The melodic framework (the tune or melody). The word literally means 'to color the mind'. Different Ragas are sung at different times of the day (e.g., Raga Bhairav in the morning, Raga Darbari at night). 
2. **Tala:** The rhythmic cycle (the beat), played on instruments like the Tabla or Mridangam.

important_entities.name: Amir Khusro
important_entities.significance: A legendary 13th-century Sufi poet and musician who introduced Persian/Arabic elements into Indian music. He is credited with inventing the **Sitar**, the **Tabla**, and the **Khayal** style of singing.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: A statement-based question often asks, 'Which of the following is true about Carnatic Music?' One option will say 'It follows the Gharana system'. This is FALSE. Only Hindustani music has Gharanas.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: S for Samaveda, S for Songs
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Out of the four Vedas, the Samaveda is entirely dedicated to chants, melodies, and songs.

exam_strategy_tips: A highly repeated SSC question: 'Which Veda is considered the primary source of Indian Classical Music?' Answer: Samaveda.
